# Preventah All Gas

> Helps a household act on the illnesses that already run in it. Pick the
> conditions a family history is relevant to, and get something concrete to
> do today, each item carrying the public-health source it came from.

Live: https://qualified-hummingbird-614.convex.site
Source: https://github.com/levithefirst/preventah-convex
Built for: the Convex All Gas Hackathon

## Not medical advice

Preventah offers general lifestyle guidance of the kind public-health
bodies publish for the whole population. It does not diagnose, predict,
treat or monitor any condition, and it is not a substitute for a
clinician. A family history raises the value of prevention and of a
conversation with one; it does not mean anyone will develop a condition.

## Public pages

- /            the purpose, and how it works
- /about       what it is and, more usefully, what it is not
- /faq         consent, invites, sources, email, solo use, data
- /privacy     every field stored, written from the schema
- /terms       hackathon project, no warranty, acceptable use
- /contact     no office, no phone; the repository is the way in

## App screens (a household is required; not useful to index)

- /today       the day's three actions and the check-in
- /conditions  the catalog picker
- /board       the live household board
- /mail        the optional morning plan
- /profile     name, household, invite link, leaving

## How it works

Conditions carry tags. Guidance items carry the same tags. An action is
shown when the two intersect, which is why a catalog of 100+ conditions
shares one curated body of guidance. Resolving a day is pure and
synchronous: the same selections and the same date always produce the
same three actions.

Sources are the World Health Organization, the NHS, the CDC and
MedlinePlus. A language model may tighten the wording of a title once a
day; it cannot introduce a drug, a dose, a lab test or a URL, and
anything that tries is rejected in favour of the original copy.

## What is not here

No advertising, no trackers, no analytics pixels, no cookie banner, no
wearables, no data sold, and no free-text field anywhere that could
become part of a health record.
